is_library.text: This is a library you import into your own code, rather than a program you run.

is_cli.text: This is a command-line tool you run from a terminal.

is_framework.text: This is a framework that wants to own the structure of your program.

is_plugin.text: This is a plugin, extension or backend for some other named tool.

is_sdk.text: This is a client or SDK for one specific external service or vendor.

is_data.text: What it ships is mainly data, assets or definitions rather than executable logic.

does_parsing.text: Its job involves reading, parsing or writing a data format.

does_network.text: Its job involves talking over a network.

does_math.text: Its job involves numerical, scientific or statistical computation.

does_testing.text: Its job is testing, linting, type-checking or otherwise checking quality.

does_packaging.text: Its job is building, packaging, installing or deploying software.

does_security.text: Its job involves security, cryptography, authentication or certificates.

does_text.text: Its job involves manipulating text or strings.

does_time.text: Its job involves dates, times, scheduling or timezones.

does_display.text: Its job involves rendering, formatting or displaying output to a human.

claims_fast.text: It claims to be fast, efficient or high-performance.

claims_simple.text: It claims to be simple, easy or lightweight.

claims_best.text: It claims to be the best, the only, or the definitive option.

positions_against.text: It defines itself against an existing alternative, as a replacement, drop-in, successor or improvement on something else.

uses_superlative.text: It uses a superlative or an intensifier such as 'blazing', 'ultimate', 'fully' or 'the most'.

names_a_vendor.text: It names a specific company, product or brand.

promises_safety.text: It makes a promise about safety, correctness, reliability or standards compliance.

is_playful.text: There is humour, wordplay or a joke in how it is written.

is_modest.text: It undersells itself, describing itself as small, simple or unambitious.

assumes_jargon.text: Understanding it requires domain jargon that an outsider would not know.

explains_purpose.text: It says what the thing is *for*, rather than only what it is.

is_full_sentence.text: It is written as a complete sentence rather than a noun phrase.

is_terse.text: It is very short, under about ten words.

has_acronym.text: It contains an acronym or initialism.

has_metaphor.text: It uses a metaphor or a figurative image.

is_imperative.text: It is phrased as an instruction or imperative to the reader.

lists_features.text: It is largely a list of features separated by commas.

for_developers.text: Its audience is programmers rather than end users.

is_infrastructure.text: It sounds like plumbing that most people will never interact with directly.

is_low_level.text: It sounds like a small low-level building block rather than a complete solution.

is_batteries_included.text: It sounds like a complete, batteries-included solution.

sounds_early.text: It sounds experimental, early or unfinished.

sounds_boring.text: It sounds reassuringly boring: unglamorous, stable, unexciting work.

hard_to_explain.text: Explaining what it does to a non-programmer would be hard.
